Hey Claude, can you help me understand the layout of the codebase? Where are the different web pages stored? Where is the database? Thanks!

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 05:40:25Z)**_

Here's the layout based on this repo's structure (Cal.diy is a Yarn/Turbo monorepo, a fork/variant of Cal.com):

## Web pages
- **`apps/web/app/`** — Next.js App Router routes (the actual page files/URLs)
- **`apps/web/modules/`** — page-level view components and web-specific logic (especially anything using tRPC hooks), organized by feature, e.g.:
  - `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`
  - `apps/web/modules/bookings/views/bookings-view.tsx`

So a URL route in `apps/web/app/` typically renders a view component that lives in `apps/web/modules/`.

## Database
- **Schema**: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` — this defines all the tables/models
- **Migrations**: `packages/prisma/migrations/`
- It's PostgreSQL, accessed via Prisma ORM. Direct Prisma access is supposed to be isolated behind **Repository classes** (e.g. `packages/features/**/repositories/*Repository.ts`) rather than scattered through business logic.

## Other key areas
- **`packages/trpc/server/routers/`** — the tRPC API layer (type-safe backend endpoints)
- **`packages/features/`** — vertical-slice feature code (services, repositories, components, tests grouped by domain like bookings, availability, etc.)
- **`packages/ui/`** — shared UI components
- **`packages/app-store/`** — third-party integrations (calendars, video, payments) — mostly `*.generated.ts` files, don't edit those by hand
- **`packages/lib/`** — low-level shared utilities (no feature/trpc dependencies allowed)
- **`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`** — English translation strings

Let me know if you want me to walk through a specific feature end-to-end (e.g., trace a booking page from route → view → tRPC → repository → DB).

# Add tooltips to remaining Event Type list-page buttons

## Context

The task is to add tooltips to the "open-calendar" (preview) button and the "open dropdown menu" (ellipsis) button on the Event Type list page, matching the two buttons in the same row that already have tooltips (the hide/show toggle and the copy-link button).

During concept location, the original hypothesis (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`) turned out to be the wrong file. That file is the header bar of the **single event-type edit page** (`/event-types/[id]`), reached via `EventType.tsx` → `EventTypeSingleLayout`. The literal string `"Link copied!"` that was used to "confirm" it also happens to live in that file, but that's a coincidence — the actual list page's equivalent toast uses a translation key (`t("link_copied")`) instead of a literal string.

The correct file, confirmed via Playwright e2e tests (`apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`) that navigate to `/event-types` and query `data-testid="preview-link-button"` and `data-testid="event-type-options-${id}"`, is:

**`apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`**

This is the list page where each row represents one event type (matches the original framing: "the one event type you'd see in the event type list").

## What's in each row today

| Button | Lines (approx) | Tooltip today | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hide/show toggle (`Switch`) | 596-619 | ✅ `<Tooltip content={...}>` | Reference pattern, no changes needed |
| Preview / "open-calendar" (`StartIcon="external-link"`, `href={calLink}`) | 624-633 | ⚠️ Has a `<Tooltip content={t("preview")}>` wrapper, but missing `side="bottom"` / `sideOffset={4}` | Renders as an anchor (`href`), so it **cannot** use the `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` Button props — same constraint documented in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` line 157 ("We have to wrap this in tooltip as it has a href which disables the tooltip on buttons"). Fix: add positioning props to the existing wrapper for consistency with the rest of the row and with the equivalent button in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (line 159-160, which already does `side="bottom" sideOffset={4}`). |
| Copy link (`StartIcon="link"`) | 635-645 | ✅ Uses `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` Button props directly | Reference pattern for non-anchor buttons |
| Ellipsis / "open dropdown menu" (`DropdownMenuTrigger` → `Button StartIcon="ellipsis"`), desktop | 670-680 | ❌ No tooltip at all | No `href`, so use the `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` Button props directly. Translation key `t("open_options")` already exists (`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` line 900) — no new translation needed. |
| Ellipsis / "open dropdown menu", mobile (`sm:hidden` variant) | 746-749 | ❌ No tooltip at all | Same fix as above, for consistency (mobile tooltips don't show on touch but keep the accessible label/consistency with desktop). |

## Changes

In `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`:

1. **Preview/"open-calendar" button (~line 624):** add `side="bottom"` and `sideOffset={4}` to the existing `<Tooltip content={t("preview")}>` wrapper so it matches the positioning of its sibling tooltips in the row.
2. **Desktop ellipsis button (~line 672-679):** add `tooltip={t("open_options")}`, `tooltipSide="bottom"`, `tooltipOffset={4}` props to the `<Button ... StartIcon="ellipsis" />` inside `DropdownMenuTrigger`.
3. **Mobile ellipsis button (~line 748):** same three props added to the `<Button type="button" variant="icon" color="secondary" StartIcon="ellipsis" />`.

No new translation strings are required — `open_options` ("Open options") already exists in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

## Verification

1. `yarn type-check:ci --force` (or scoped to the changed file) to confirm the added props type-check against the shared `Button`/`Tooltip` component APIs.
2. Run the app locally (`yarn dev`), go to `/event-types`, hover over the preview and "..." buttons in a row and confirm tooltips appear, positioned below the button like the existing hide-toggle/copy-link tooltips.
3. Run `apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts` (or at least confirm `data-testid="preview-link-button"` and `data-testid="event-type-options-*"` selectors still resolve) to make sure adding tooltip props didn't change the DOM structure e2e tests rely on.

Good, confirmed on both counts. No code written — just explaining.

## Why the preview button's tooltip can't use the `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` props

Look at the shared `Button` component: `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`.

It decides how to render itself right here:

```ts
const isLink = typeof props.href !== "undefined";
...
if (isLink) {
  return (
    <Link ...>
      {buttonContent}
    </Link>
  );
}

return (
  <Wrapper tooltip={props.tooltip} tooltipSide={tooltipSide} tooltipOffset={tooltipOffset} ...>
    <button ...>{buttonContent}</button>
  </Wrapper>
);
```

The `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` props are only ever consumed by `Wrapper` (defined at the bottom of the file), which conditionally wraps the button in `<Tooltip>`. But `Wrapper` is **only used in the plain `<button>` branch**. When `href` is set, `isLink` is `true`, and the component takes the completely separate `<Link>` return path — which never touches `Wrapper` at all. So if you pass `tooltip="foo"` to a `Button` that also has `href`, that prop is silently ignored; nothing crashes, no tooltip ever appears.

That's exactly what the comment in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (line 157) is warning about: *"We have to wrap this in tooltip as it has a href which disables the tooltip on buttons."* The workaround is to manually wrap the `<Button href=... />` in a `<Tooltip>` component yourself, which is what both the preview button in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` and the one in `event-types-listing-view.tsx` already do. So the preview button does have a working tooltip today — it's just implemented via the manual `<Tooltip>` wrapper (the only mechanism that works for link-buttons) rather than via props.

Good catch — that is a real localization bug. Compare:

- `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx:641` → `showToast(t("link_copied"), "success");` — correctly translated (translation key `"link_copied": "Link copied!"` exists at `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:910`).

So on the single event-type edit page, a non-English user would still see "Link copied!" in English, while the list page correctly shows the localized string. This is a small, separate, legitimate bug independent of the tooltip task.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 06:51:36Z)**_

No code written — I updated the plan doc's follow-up notes with this new bug, but let me explain what's going on.

## Why the preview button's tooltip doesn't actually appear (this is a real bug, not just a positioning issue)

This traces directly to that comment. Look at how `Button` decides what to render, in `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`:

```ts
const isLink = typeof props.href !== "undefined";
...
if (isLink) {
  return (
    <Link {...passThroughProps} className={buttonClassName} onClick={handleClick}>
      {buttonContent}
    </Link>
  );  // <-- no ref passed here
}

return (
  <Wrapper tooltip={props.tooltip} ...>
    <button ref={forwardedRef} ...>{buttonContent}</button>  // <-- ref IS passed here
  </Wrapper>
);
```

`Button` is created with `forwardRef`, meaning it receives a `ref` from whoever renders it, as a second function argument (`forwardedRef`). In the plain-button branch, that ref gets attached to the real `<button>` DOM element. In the `<Link>` branch — the one taken whenever `href` is set — `forwardedRef` is simply never used. It's dropped on the floor.

Now here's why that breaks the tooltip. `Tooltip` (in `packages/ui/components/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`) is built on Radix UI:

```tsx
<TooltipPrimitive.Trigger asChild>{children}</TooltipPrimitive.Trigger>
```

`asChild` is a Radix pattern: instead of rendering its own wrapper element, `Trigger` clones whatever single child you give it (here, your `<Button href=... />`) and injects extra props onto that clone — including a `ref`, plus hover/focus event handlers. Radix needs that ref to point at a **real DOM node** so it can measure its position on screen (to know where to draw the tooltip bubble) and track pointer enter/leave against it.

Since `Button`'s `<Link>` branch never forwards that injected ref anywhere, the ref stays `null` — it never resolves to an actual `<a>` element in the DOM. Radix's positioning logic (built on Popper/floating-ui) has no anchor element to measure, so the tooltip content has nothing to position itself against and effectively never renders. That matches exactly what you're seeing: no visual difference at all, not even a misplaced tooltip.

This is a **pre-existing bug that affects every `<Tooltip><Button href=... /></Tooltip>` in the codebase**, not something specific to this file. Importantly, it also means my plan's proposed fix for the preview button (just adding `side="bottom"`/`sideOffset={4}` to the existing wrapper) wouldn't have actually fixed anything — those are just positioning knobs on a tooltip that isn't rendering in the first place. I've noted this in the plan file as a blocker to resolve/discuss before touching that button.

## The "type conflict" comment

```ts
export type ButtonProps = ButtonBaseProps &
  (
    | (Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "onClick" | "ref"> & LinkProps)
    | (Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["button"], "onClick" | "ref"> & { href?: never })
  );
```

Some vocabulary first:
- **Anchor element** = the actual HTML `<a href="...">` tag — the real DOM element browsers use for hyperlinks. It's a different HTML element from `<button>`, with different valid attributes (e.g. `href`, `target`, `rel` make sense on `<a>`, not on `<button>`).
- **`ref`** = React's escape hatch for getting a direct handle to the real underlying DOM node (or class component instance) instead of only interacting through props/state. You use it when you need to do something imperative — call `.focus()`, measure `.getBoundingClientRect()`, or, as here, let a library like Radix attach listeners directly to the actual element.

`ButtonProps` is a TypeScript union: either "anchor-shaped props" (must include `href`, from `LinkProps`) *or* "button-shaped props" (`href` explicitly disallowed via `href?: never`). Two consequences:

1. **The two branches expect different, incompatible prop sets.** `<button>` doesn't accept `href` at all in its type; `Link` requires it. If the code tried to pick the tag dynamically (`const Tag = isLink ? Link : "button"`) and spread one shared `passThroughProps` object onto it, TypeScript can't prove which half of the union `passThroughProps` actually is at that point (the `isLink` boolean is a runtime check, not something TS automatically uses to narrow the type of `props`/`passThroughProps` for you), so it would flag a mismatch. Writing two fully separate `if (isLink) return <Link/>; return <button/>;` branches sidesteps that — each branch only ever has to satisfy one half of the union.

2. **The `ref` types genuinely differ.** A `<button>` ref is `React.Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`; an anchor/`Link` ref is `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>`. `Button`'s `forwardedRef` is typed as `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement>` to cover both cases — but you can't just hand that combined-type ref to a single call site that only accepts one specific element type without TypeScript complaining (or without an unsafe cast, which the project's rules explicitly forbid — no `as any`).

So the comment is explaining *why* the code is split into two returns (a real TypeScript constraint), but the accompanying assumption — "Link manages its own anchor element, so we don't need to pass ref to it" — turns out to be wrong in practice for this use case. Next's `Link` *does* support forwarding a ref down to its underlying `<a>`; the `Button` component just never wires it up in that branch. That gap is what's silently breaking your tooltip.

````markdown
# Add tooltips to remaining Event Type list-page buttons

## Context

The task is to add tooltips to the "open-calendar" (preview) button and the "open dropdown menu" (ellipsis) button on the Event Type list page (`/event-types`), matching the two buttons in the same row that already have tooltips (the hide/show toggle and the copy-link button).

During concept location, the original hypothesis (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`) turned out to be the wrong file — that's the header bar of the *single* event-type edit page (`/event-types/[id]`). The correct file, confirmed via Playwright e2e tests (`apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`, which navigate to `/event-types` and query `data-testid="preview-link-button"` / `data-testid="event-type-options-${id}"`), is:

**`apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`**

While investigating, we discovered the preview button's existing `<Tooltip>` wrapper doesn't actually display anything, in dev or prod. Root cause: `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`'s `Button` component renders an entirely separate `<Link>` branch when `href` is set, and that branch never forwards the component's `forwardedRef` to the underlying `<a>`. Radix's `Tooltip` (`TooltipPrimitive.Trigger asChild`) needs that ref to find the real DOM node to anchor/position itself against; without it, the tooltip has nothing to measure and never renders. This affects every `<Tooltip><Button href=... /></Tooltip>` in the codebase, not just this row. Since the tooltip feature is meaningless without this fix, we're doing both in one PR (see decision below).

## Decisions made

```text
1	# Add tooltips to remaining Event Type list-page buttons
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The task is to add tooltips to the "open-calendar" (preview) button and the "open dropdown menu" (ellipsis) button on the Event Type list page (`/event-types`), matching the two buttons in the same row that already have tooltips (the hide/show toggle and the copy-link button).
6	
7	During concept location, the original hypothesis (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`) turned out to be the wrong file — that's the header bar of the *single* event-type edit page (`/event-types/[id]`). The correct file, confirmed via Playwright e2e tests (`apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`, which navigate to `/event-types` and query `data-testid="preview-link-button"` / `data-testid="event-type-options-${id}"`), is:
8	
9	**`apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`**
10	
11	While investigating, we discovered the preview button's existing `<Tooltip>` wrapper doesn't actually display anything, in dev or prod. Root cause: `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`'s `Button` component renders an entirely separate `<Link>` branch when `href` is set, and that branch never forwards the component's `forwardedRef` to the underlying `<a>`. Radix's `Tooltip` (`TooltipPrimitive.Trigger asChild`) needs that ref to find the real DOM node to anchor/position itself against; without it, the tooltip has nothing to measure and never renders. This affects every `<Tooltip><Button href=... /></Tooltip>` in the codebase, not just this row. Since the tooltip feature is meaningless without this fix, we're doing both in one PR (see decision below).
12	
13	## Decisions made
14	
15	- **One PR** containing both the `Button.tsx` ref fix and the two tooltip additions — splitting them would leave an intermediate PR where the tooltip props don't actually do anything.
16	- **Add an e2e test.** No test in this repo currently hovers an element and asserts a tooltip becomes visible (`apps/web/playwright` has zero `.hover()` calls) — that's a real gap, since it's exactly the class of bug (renders fine in the DOM, doesn't actually display in a real browser) a unit test can't catch. We're adding one small Playwright test as the reliable regression guard.
17	
18	## Changes
19	
20	### 1. `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx` — fix ref forwarding for link-rendered buttons
21	
22	In the `isLink` branch (~line 331-341), add ref forwarding to `<Link>`:
23	
24	```tsx
25	if (isLink) {
26	  return (
27	    <Link
28	      {...(passThroughProps as Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "onClick" | "ref"> & LinkProps)}
29	      ref={forwardedRef as React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>}
30	      shallow={shallow && shallow}
31	      className={buttonClassName}
32	      onClick={handleClick}>
33	      {buttonContent}
34	    </Link>
35	  );
36	}
37	```
38	
39	- The cast is required (and is a legitimate, narrow type assertion — not the banned `as any`): `forwardedRef` is typed `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement>` because `Button` is declared as `forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>`, but a `RefObject`'s `current` property is invariant in TypeScript, so the wider union type isn't automatically assignable to the narrower `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` that `Link` expects.
40	- Verified this works at runtime: repo is on Next.js 16.2.3, where `next/link`'s `Link` renders a real `<a>` directly and forwards `ref` to it (no `legacyBehavior` child-anchor requirement).
41	- Verified this doesn't break the existing `tooltip`/`DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` composition pattern used for the ellipsis button (see change #3) — `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:128-133` already does `<DialogTrigger asChild><Button tooltip={t("edit")} .../></DialogTrigger>`, proving nested Radix `*Trigger asChild` + `Button`'s own internal tooltip wrapper is a working, precedented pattern in this codebase.
42	- Checked for existing call sites that pass both `href` and `ref` to `Button` (which previously had their ref silently dropped, so a type mismatch there could newly surface). Found none in a codebase search. `yarn type-check:ci --force` is the safety net if any exist elsewhere — a real mismatch will now surface as a compile error instead of a silent no-op, which is a correct outcome, not a new class of bug.
43	
44	### 2. `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx` — position the preview tooltip
45	
46	Preview/"open-calendar" button (~line 624): add `side="bottom"` and `sideOffset={4}` to the existing `<Tooltip content={t("preview")}>` wrapper, matching the positioning already used for its sibling tooltips in the row and the equivalent button in `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (line 159-160).
47	
48	### 3. Same file — add tooltip to the ellipsis "open dropdown menu" button
49	
50	Two occurrences (desktop ~line 672-679, mobile ~line 748) of the `<Button ... StartIcon="ellipsis" />` inside `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`. Add directly as Button props (no `href`, so the normal prop path works — same pattern as the existing copy-link button and the `DateOverrideList.tsx` precedent above):
51	
52	```tsx
53	tooltip={t("open_options")}
54	tooltipSide="bottom"
55	tooltipOffset={4}
56	```
57	
58	No new translation needed — `"open_options": "Open options"` already exists at `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:900`.
59	
60	## Tests
61	
62	### Unit test — `packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`
63

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 08:13:22Z)**_

Before I write this, I need to flag something — wrapping the ellipsis button in `<Tooltip>` would actually reintroduce the same class of bug we just fixed, just in the `DropdownMenu` instead of the `Tooltip`. Let me explain why the ellipsis button is a special case that the "match the file convention" reasoning doesn't actually apply to.

**The problem:** the ellipsis button isn't a standalone button like preview/copy-link — it's the child of `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`:

```tsx
<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild data-testid={...}>
  <Button ... StartIcon="ellipsis" />
</DropdownMenuTrigger>
```

`asChild` clones its immediate child and injects a `ref` plus props (`onClick`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `id`, etc.) directly onto it, so Radix can wire up the dropdown's open/close behavior and positioning to a real DOM node — same mechanism as the `Tooltip`/`Button`/`href` bug we just fixed.

If I make the child `<Tooltip><Button/></Tooltip>` instead of `<Button/>` directly, two things break:

1. **`Tooltip` (in `packages/ui/components/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`) is a plain function component, not wrapped in `React.forwardRef`.** When `DropdownMenuTrigger`'s `asChild` tries to attach its ref to `Tooltip`, React can't — function components can't receive refs. The ref stays `null`, and `DropdownMenuTrigger` loses its anchor for positioning the menu.
2. **`Tooltip` doesn't forward its extra props to `children` either** — look at its implementation: it destructures its own named props and spreads the rest (`...props`) only onto `TooltipPrimitive.Content` (the tooltip bubble), never onto `{children}` (the trigger). So the `onClick`/`aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded` that `DropdownMenuTrigger` needs on the actual button would silently land nowhere useful — breaking click handling and accessibility semantics for opening the dropdown.

**Why `Button`'s `tooltip` prop avoids this:** `Button` *is* a proper `forwardRef` component, and in its non-link branch it spreads `passThroughProps` (which includes whatever `DropdownMenuTrigger` injected) and attaches `ref={forwardedRef}` directly onto the real `<button>` element — then wraps that in its own internal `Tooltip` further down, without disturbing the outer composition. This is exactly the working precedent I found earlier: `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:128-133` does `<DialogTrigger asChild><Button tooltip={t("edit")} .../></DialogTrigger>` for this exact reason.

So: the "match this file's convention" reasoning holds for preview/copy-link (standalone buttons), but not for the ellipsis button, which is uniquely nested inside another `asChild` trigger. For that one, using the `tooltip` prop is the *correct* choice, not an inconsistency.

**Title:**
```
feat(event-types): add tooltips to preview and dropdown-menu buttons
```

**Body:**
```markdown
## Summary

Closes #16. Adds tooltips to the remaining icon-only action buttons on the Event Types list page (`/event-types`) that didn't already have them — the "preview" (view event) button and the "..." dropdown-menu button — matching the tooltips already present on the hide/show toggle and copy-link buttons in the same row.

While implementing this, we found the preview button's tooltip was actually broken in dev/prod despite already being wrapped in `<Tooltip>`: `Button` never forwarded its `ref` to the underlying `<a>` when rendered with `href`, so Radix's `Tooltip` had no real DOM node to anchor/position itself against and silently never displayed. Fixing that is included here since the dropdown-menu tooltip's own correctness also depends on `Button`'s ref-forwarding behavior (see commit 2).

## Changes

- **`packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`**: forward `ref` to `<Link>`'s underlying anchor element when `href` is set, so `Tooltip`/other `asChild`-based consumers can find a real DOM node to attach to.
- **`apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`**: add an "Open options" tooltip to the ellipsis dropdown-menu button (desktop + mobile). Uses `Button`'s `tooltip` prop rather than this file's usual `<Tooltip>` wrap, because this button is the child of `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` — wrapping it in `<Tooltip>` (a non-`forwardRef` component that doesn't forward extra props to its trigger child) would silently break the dropdown's own ref/click handling.
- **Tests**: new unit tests for `Button`'s ref forwarding (`packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`), and a new e2e test that hovers the preview and "..." buttons on `/event-types` and asserts a tooltip becomes visible (`apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`).

## Out of scope

`EventTypeLayout.tsx` (the single event-type edit page) has an unrelated, pre-existing bug — a hardcoded, untranslated `"Link copied!"` toast string instead of `t("link_copied")`. Tracked separately, not fixed in this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (`packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`)
- [ ] E2E test passes (`apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`)
- [x] Manually verified in browser: hovering the preview and "..." buttons on `/event-types` now shows tooltips
- [ ] `yarn type-check:ci --force`
- [ ] `yarn biome check --write .`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

1	# Cal.diy Development Guide for AI Agents
2	
3	You are a senior Cal.diy engineer working in a Yarn/Turbo monorepo. You prioritize type safety, security, and small, reviewable diffs.
4	
5	## Do
6	
7	- Use `select` instead of `include` in Prisma queries for performance and security
8	- Use `import type { X }` for TypeScript type imports
9	- Use early returns to reduce nesting: `if (!booking) return null;`
10	- Use `ErrorWithCode` for errors in non-tRPC files (services, repositories, utilities); use `TRPCError` only in tRPC routers
11	- Use conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`
12	- Create PRs in draft mode by default
13	- Run `yarn type-check:ci --force` before concluding CI failures are unrelated to your changes
14	- Import directly from source files, not barrel files (e.g., `@calcom/ui/components/button` not `@calcom/ui`)
15	- Add translations to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` for all UI strings
16	- Use `date-fns` or native `Date` instead of Day.js when timezone awareness isn't needed
17	- Put permission checks in `page.tsx`, never in `layout.tsx`
18	- Use `ast-grep` for searching if available; otherwise use `rg` (ripgrep), then fall back to `grep`

24	
25	- Never use `as any` - use proper type-safe solutions instead
26	- Never expose `credential.key` field in API responses or queries
27	- Never commit secrets or API keys
28	- Never modify `*.generated.ts` files directly - they're created by app-store-cli
29	- Never put business logic in repositories - that belongs in Services
30	- Never use barrel imports from index.ts files
31	- Never skip running type checks before pushing

33	- Never add comments that simply restate what the code does (e.g., `// Get the user` above a `getUser()` call)
34	
35	## PR Size Guidelines
36	
37	Large PRs are difficult to review, prone to errors, and slow down the development process. Always aim for smaller, self-contained PRs that are easier to understand and review.
38	
39	### Size Limits
40	
41	- **Lines changed**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code (additions + deletions)
42	- **Files changed**: Keep PRs under 10 code files
43	- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should do one thing well
44	
45	**Note**: These limits apply to code files only. Non-code files like documentation (README.md, CHANGELOG.md), lock files (yarn.lock, package-lock.json), and auto-generated files are excluded from the count.
46	
47	### How to Split Large Changes
48	
49	When a task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs:
50	
51	1. **By layer**: Separate database/schema changes, backend logic, and frontend UI into different PRs
52	2. **By feature component**: Split a feature into its constituent parts (e.g., API endpoint PR, then UI PR, then integration PR)
53	3. **By refactor vs feature**: Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new functionality
54	4. **By dependency order**: Create PRs in the order they can be merged (base infrastructure first, then features that depend on it)
55	
56	### Examples of Good PR Splits
57	
58	**Instead of one large "Add booking notifications" PR:**
59	- PR 1: Add notification preferences schema and migration
60	- PR 2: Add notification service and API endpoints
61	- PR 3: Add notification UI components
62	- PR 4: Integrate notifications into booking flow
63	
64	**Instead of one large "Refactor calendar sync" PR:**
65	- PR 1: Extract calendar sync logic into dedicated service
66	- PR 2: Add new calendar provider abstraction
67	- PR 3: Migrate existing providers to new abstraction
68	- PR 4: Add new calendar provider support
69	
70	### Benefits of Smaller PRs
71	
72	- Faster review cycles and quicker feedback
73	- Easier to identify and fix issues
74	- Lower risk of merge conflicts
75	- Simpler to revert if problems arise
76	- Better git history and easier debugging
77	
78	## Commands
79	
80	See [agents/commands.md](agents/commands.md) for full reference. Key commands:
81	
82	```bash
83	yarn type-check:ci --force  # Type check (always run before pushing)
84	yarn biome check --write .  # Lint and format
85	TZ=UTC yarn test            # Run unit tests
86	yarn prisma generate        # Regenerate types after schema changes
87	```
88	
89	
90	## Boundaries
91	
92	### Always do
93	- Run type check on changed files before committing
94	- Run relevant tests before pushing
95	- Use `select` in Prisma queries
96	- Follow conventional commits for PR titles
97	- Run Biome before pushing
98	
99	### Ask first
100	- Adding new dependencies
101	- Schema changes to `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`
102	- Changes affecting multiple packages
103	- Deleting files
104	- Running full build or E2E suites
105	
106	### Never do
107	- Commit secrets, API keys, or `.env` files
108	- Expose `credential.key` in any query
109	- Use `as any` type casting
110	- Force push or rebase shared branches
111	- Modify generated files directly

113	## Project Structure
114	
115	```
116	apps/web/                    # Main Next.js application
117	packages/prisma/             # Database schema (schema.prisma) and migrations
118	packages/trpc/               # tRPC API layer (routers in server/routers/)
119	packages/ui/                 # Shared UI components

121	packages/app-store/          # Third-party integrations
122	packages/lib/                # Shared utilities

127	- Database schema: `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`

132	## Tech Stack
133	
134	- **Framework**: Next.js 13+ (App Router in some areas)
135	- **Language**: TypeScript (strict)
136	- **Database**: PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM
137	- **API**: tRPC for type-safe APIs
138	- **Auth**: NextAuth.js
139	- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS
140	- **Testing**: Vitest (unit), Playwright (E2E)
141	- **i18n**: next-i18next

143	## Code Examples
144	
145	### Good error handling
146	
147	```typescript
148	// Good - Descriptive error with context
149	throw new Error(`Unable to create booking: User ${userId} has no available time slots for ${date}`);
150	
151	// Bad - Generic error
152	throw new Error("Booking failed");
153	```
154	
155	For which error class to use (`ErrorWithCode` vs `TRPCError`) and concrete examples, see [quality-error-handling](agents/rules/quality-error-handling.md).
156	
157	### Good Prisma query
158	
159	```typescript
160	// Good - Use select for performance and security
161	const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({
162	  select: {
163	    id: true,
164	    title: true,
165	    user: {
166	      select: {
167	        id: true,
168	        name: true,
169	        email: true,
170	      }
171	    }
172	  }
173	});
174	
175	// Bad - Include fetches all fields including sensitive ones
176	const booking = await prisma.booking.findFirst({
177	  include: { user: true }
178	});
179	```
180	
181	### Good imports
182	
183	```typescript
184	// Good - Type imports and direct paths
185	import type { User } from "@prisma/client";
186	import { Button } from "@calcom/ui/components/button";
187	
188	// Bad - Regular import for types, barrel imports
189	import { User } from "@prisma/client";
190	import { Button } from "@calcom/ui";
191	```
192	
193	### API v2 Imports (apps/api/v2)
194	
195	When importing from `@calcom/features` or `@calcom/trpc` into `apps/api/v2`, **do not import directly** because the API v2 app's `tsconfig.json` doesn't have path mappings for these modules, which causes "module not found" errors.
196	
197	Instead, re-export from `packages/platform/libraries/index.ts` and import from `@calcom/platform-libraries`:
198	
199	```typescript
200	// Step 1: In packages/platform/libraries/index.ts, add the export
201	export { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
202	
203	// Step 2: In apps/api/v2, import from platform-libraries
204	import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/platform-libraries";
205	
206	// Bad - Direct import causes module not found error in apps/api/v2
207	import { ProfileRepository } from "@calcom/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository";
208	```

10	
11	While investigating, we discovered the preview button's existing `<Tooltip>` wrapper doesn't actually display anything, in dev or prod. Root cause: `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`'s `Button` component renders an entirely separate `<Link>` branch when `href` is set, and that branch never forwards the component's `forwardedRef` to the underlying `<a>`. Radix's `Tooltip` (`TooltipPrimitive.Trigger asChild`) needs that ref to find the real DOM node to anchor/position itself against; without it, the tooltip has nothing to measure and never renders. This affects every `<Tooltip><Button href=... /></Tooltip>` in the codebase, not just this row. Since the tooltip feature is meaningless without this fix, we're doing both in one PR (see decision below).
12	
13	## Decisions made
14	
15	- **One PR** containing both the `Button.tsx` ref fix and the two tooltip additions — splitting them would leave an intermediate PR where the tooltip props don't actually do anything.
16	- **Add an e2e test.** No test in this repo currently hovers an element and asserts a tooltip becomes visible (`apps/web/playwright` has zero `.hover()` calls) — that's a real gap, since it's exactly the class of bug (renders fine in the DOM, doesn't actually display in a real browser) a unit test can't catch. We're adding one small Playwright test as the reliable regression guard.
17	
18	## Changes
19	
20	### 1. `packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx` — fix ref forwarding for link-rendered buttons
21	
22	In the `isLink` branch (~line 331-341), add ref forwarding to `<Link>`:
23	
24	```tsx
25	if (isLink) {
26	  return (
27	    <Link
28	      {...(passThroughProps as Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "onClick" | "ref"> & LinkProps)}
29	      ref={forwardedRef as React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>}
30	      shallow={shallow && shallow}
31	      className={buttonClassName}
32	      onClick={handleClick}>
33	      {buttonContent}
34	    </Link>
35	  );
36	}
37	```
38	
39	- The cast is required (and is a legitimate, narrow type assertion — not the banned `as any`): `forwardedRef` is typed `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement>` because `Button` is declared as `forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement | HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>`, but a `RefObject`'s `current` property is invariant in TypeScript, so the wider union type isn't automatically assignable to the narrower `React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` that `Link` expects.
40	- Verified this works at runtime: repo is on Next.js 16.2.3, where `next/link`'s `Link` renders a real `<a>` directly and forwards `ref` to it (no `legacyBehavior` child-anchor requirement).
41	- Verified this doesn't break the existing `tooltip`/`DropdownMenuTrigger asChild` composition pattern used for the ellipsis button (see change #3) — `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:128-133` already does `<DialogTrigger asChild><Button tooltip={t("edit")} .../></DialogTrigger>`, proving nested Radix `*Trigger asChild` + `Button`'s own internal tooltip wrapper is a working, precedented pattern in this codebase.
42	- Checked for existing call sites that pass both `href` and `ref` to `Button` (which previously had their ref silently dropped, so a type mismatch there could newly surface). Found none in a codebase search. `yarn type-check:ci --force` is the safety net if any exist elsewhere — a real mismatch will now surface as a compile error instead of a silent no-op, which is a correct outcome, not a new class of bug.
43	
44	### 2. `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx` — preview tooltip: no change
45	
46	Correction: `side="bottom"`/`sideOffset={4}` is a pattern from `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (the single event-type edit page), not from this file. Every existing tooltip in this row (hide-toggle at ~line 600, copy-link at ~line 635) uses a bare `<Tooltip content={...}>` with no `side`/`sideOffset`, defaulting to Radix's `top` placement. Decision: leave the preview button's `<Tooltip content={t("preview")}>` untouched so it stays consistent with its row siblings — no code change needed here.
47	
48	### 3. Same file — add tooltip to the ellipsis "open dropdown menu" button
49	
50	Two occurrences (desktop ~line 672-679, mobile ~line 748) of the `<Button ... StartIcon="ellipsis" />` inside `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`.
51	
52	**Must use `Button`'s `tooltip` prop directly here, NOT the external `<Tooltip>` wrap** used elsewhere in this file — even though the wrap is this file's usual convention for standalone buttons. Reason: this button is the immediate child of `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`, which clones its child and injects a `ref` + props (`onClick`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, etc.) onto it so Radix can wire up the dropdown. `Tooltip` (`packages/ui/components/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`) is a plain function component, not `forwardRef`, and it only forwards its extra props to `TooltipPrimitive.Content` (the bubble), never to `children` (the trigger) — so wrapping `<Tooltip><Button/></Tooltip>` here would silently break `DropdownMenuTrigger`'s ref/click-handling, the same bug class we just fixed in `Button`, but for the dropdown menu instead. `Button`'s `tooltip` prop avoids this because `Button` is a proper `forwardRef` component that spreads injected props and the ref straight onto the real `<button>` element before wrapping it in its own internal tooltip — matching the working precedent at `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:128-133` (`<DialogTrigger asChild><Button tooltip={t("edit")} .../></DialogTrigger>`).
53	
54	No explicit `tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset`, so it defaults to `top`, matching the rest of the row:
55	
56	```tsx
57	tooltip={t("open_options")}
58	```
59	
60	No new translation needed — `"open_options": "Open options"` already exists at `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:900`.
61	
62	## Tests
63	
64	### Unit test — `packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`
65	
66	Note: the existing test suites in this file are entirely wrapped in `describe.skip(...)` (there's a `TODO: (SEAN) Fix tests for button component` comment saying they're broken due to a vitest/RTL version change). A new test added inside those skipped blocks would silently never run. So: add a **new, separate, non-skipped `describe` block** specifically for this regression, rather than touching the existing skipped suites (out of scope to fix those here).
67	
68	Test: render `<Button href="/test" ref={ref} />` with a `React.createRef<HTMLAnchorElement>()`, assert `ref.current` is a real anchor element (e.g. `ref.current?.tagName === "A"`). This is a DOM-structure/ref assertion, which jsdom handles reliably — unlike tooltip *visibility*, which depends on real layout that jsdom doesn't compute (this is part of why the bug shipped silently in the first place).
69	
70	### E2E test — `apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`
71	
72	Add a small test: go to `/event-types`, hover the preview button (`data-testid="preview-link-button"`) and assert a tooltip with the expected text becomes visible; same for the ellipsis button (`data-testid="event-type-options-${id}"`). This is a new pattern for this test file/repo — no existing test to copy verbatim — so write it using Playwright's standard `locator.hover()` + `page.getByRole("tooltip")`/text assertion.
73	
74	## Verification
75	
76	1. `yarn type-check:ci --force` — confirm the `Button.tsx` ref fix and the new tooltip props all type-check.
77	2. `TZ=UTC yarn test` (or scoped to `packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`) — new unit test passes.
78	3. Run the app locally (`yarn dev`), go to `/event-types`, hover the preview and "..." buttons, confirm both tooltips now actually appear, positioned below the button.
79	4. Run the new/updated `apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts` e2e test (needs the `ready-for-e2e` PR label to run in CI, per this repo's e2e-gating rule).
80	5. `yarn biome check --write .` before pushing.
81
```

      {EndIcon && (
        <>
          {variant === "fab" ? (
            <>
              <Icon name={EndIcon} className="hidden h-4 w-4 shrink-0 stroke-[1.5px] md:inline-flex" />
              <Icon name="plus" data-testid="plus" className="inline h-6 w-6 shrink-0 md:hidden" />
            </>
          ) : (
            <Icon
              name={EndIcon}
              className={classNames(
                "shrink-0",
                loading ? "invisible" : "visible",
                "group-[:not(div):active]:translate-y-[0.5px]",
                variant === "icon" && "h-4 w-4",
                variant === "button" && "h-4 w-4 stroke-[1.5px] "
              )}
            />
          )}
        </>
      )}
    </>
  );

  // Render Link or button separately to avoid type conflicts: `<a>` and `<button>`
  // accept different, incompatible props (e.g. href) and ref target types.
  if (isLink) {
    return (
      <Link
        {...(passThroughProps as Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["a"], "href" | "onClick" | "ref"> & LinkProps)}
        ref={forwardedRef as React.Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>}
        shallow={shallow && shallow}
        className={buttonClassName}
        onClick={handleClick}>
        {buttonContent}
      </Link>
    );
  }

  return (
    <Wrapper
      data-testid="wrapper"
      tooltip={props.tooltip}
      tooltipSide={tooltipSide}
      tooltipOffset={tooltipOffset}
      tooltipClassName={tooltipClassName}>
      <button
        {...(passThroughProps as Omit<JSX.IntrinsicElements["button"], "onClick" | "ref">)}
        ref={forwardedRef as React.Ref<HTMLButtonElement>}
        disabled={disabled}
        type={type as "button" | "submit" | "reset"}
        className={buttonClassName}
        onClick={handleClick}>
        {buttonContent}
      </button>
    </Wrapper>
  );
});

const Wrapper = ({
  children,
  tooltip,
  tooltipSide,
  tooltipOffset,
  tooltipClassName,
}: {
  tooltip?: string | React.ReactNode;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  tooltipSide?: "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left";
  tooltipOffset?: number;
  tooltipClassName?: string;
}) => {
  if (!tooltip) {
    return <>{children}</>;
  }

  return (
    <Tooltip
      data-testid="tooltip"
      className={tooltipClassName}
      content={tooltip}
      side={tooltipSide}
      sideOffset={tooltipOffset}>
      {children}
    </Tooltip>
  );
};

Button.displayName = "Button";
```

```text
"use client";

import * as TooltipPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-tooltip";
import React from "react";

import classNames from "@calcom/ui/classNames";

export function Tooltip({
  children,
  content,
  open,
  defaultOpen,
  onOpenChange,
  delayDuration,
  side = "top",
  ...props
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  content: React.ReactNode;
  delayDuration?: number;
  open?: boolean;
  defaultOpen?: boolean;
  side?: "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left";
  onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void;
} & TooltipPrimitive.TooltipContentProps) {
  const Content = (
    <TooltipPrimitive.Content
      {...props}
      className={classNames(
        "calcom-tooltip",
        side === "top" && "-mt-7",
        side === "left" && "mr-2",
        side === "right" && "ml-2",
        "bg-inverted text-inverted relative z-50 rounded-sm px-2 py-1 text-xs font-semibold shadow-lg",
        props.className && `${props.className}`
      )}
      side={side}
      align="center">
      {content}
    </TooltipPrimitive.Content>
  );

  return (
    <TooltipPrimitive.Root
      delayDuration={delayDuration || 50}
      open={open}
      defaultOpen={defaultOpen}
      onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>
      <TooltipPrimitive.Trigger asChild>{children}</TooltipPrimitive.Trigger>
      <TooltipPrimitive.Portal>{Content}</TooltipPrimitive.Portal>
    </TooltipPrimitive.Root>
  );
}

export default Tooltip;

Author: Dylan Han <dchan01@wm.edu>

    fix: forward ref to anchor element in Button when href is set
    
    Button rendered a separate <Link> branch when href was provided but
    never attached the component's forwardedRef to it. Radix's Tooltip
    (and any other consumer using asChild) relies on that ref to find the
    real DOM node to anchor/position itself against, so tooltips wrapped
    around href-Buttons silently never displayed in the browser, even
    though they rendered without error in tests.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 09:29:08Z)**_

## `yarn type-check:ci --force`

This runs `turbo run type-check:ci --log-prefix=none` (that's the actual script behind the `yarn type-check:ci` alias in the root `package.json`), and `--force` is an extra flag you pass through to `turbo`.

- **What `type-check:ci` does per package**: each package defines its own `type-check:ci` script — in `apps/web/package.json` it's `tsc-absolute --pretty --noEmit`. That's plain TypeScript's compiler in check-only mode: `--noEmit` means it doesn't write out any `.js` files, it just type-checks the code and reports errors; `--pretty` gives readable colored output; `tsc-absolute` is a thin wrapper around `tsc` that rewrites reported file paths to absolute paths (useful for CI tooling/editors that need to jump to the exact file, rather than a path relative to whichever package `tsc` happened to run from).
- **What `turbo` adds**: this is a monorepo with dozens of packages, so `turbo run type-check:ci` runs that script across every package that defines it, in the correct dependency order (per `turbo.json`, `type-check:ci` `dependsOn: ["@calcom/trpc#build"]` — since many packages import types generated by `@calcom/trpc`, that package gets built first).
- **What `--force` does**: `turbo` normally caches task results — if a package's inputs haven't changed since the last successful run, it skips re-running the task and just replays the cached output (you saw this in our commits: `@calcom/app-store-cli:build: cache hit, replaying logs`). `--force` bypasses that cache entirely and re-runs every package's type-check for real. This matters for a final pre-push check because you want a guaranteed, fresh answer — not a possibly-stale cached "it passed" from before your latest edits.

## `yarn biome check --write .`

Biome is this repo's linter + formatter (replacing what would otherwise be separate ESLint + Prettier tools). `biome check` is Biome's combined command — in one pass it runs:
- the **linter** (catches bugs/style issues, per rules configured in `biome.json`),
- the **formatter** (enforces consistent spacing/line width/quotes — this repo's config: 110-char line width, 2-space indent, LF line endings),
- and **assists** like `organizeImports` (auto-sorts import statements into the group order defined in `biome.json`, e.g. mocks first, then external packages, then `@calcom/**`, then relative imports).

`--write` tells it to actually apply every fix it's capable of making automatically (formatting, import order, and any lint rule that has a safe auto-fix) rather than just reporting them as diagnostics. `.` scopes it to the whole repo starting from the current directory.

That's the literal `yarn biome check --write .` command from `AGENTS.md`'s reference list — as I flagged earlier, I deliberately didn't run it repo-wide on our branch, since doing so would reformat every file Biome has an opinion on, not just the ones we touched, which would blow up our diff into something unrelated to this PR. What actually ran on our commits was the `pre-commit` hook (`lint-staged` → `biome lint --reporter summary --config-path=biome-staged.json`), which is a narrower check scoped to just the staged files.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 09:36:47Z)**_

Sure — walking through the reasoning again for the hover-test fix specifically (the code change, not the earlier `Button.tsx`/tooltip explanations from before).

**The bug in the test as currently written:**

```ts
const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]');

await page.locator("[data-testid=preview-link-button]").first().hover();
await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
await expect(tooltip).toHaveText("Preview");

await page.locator(`[data-testid=event-type-options-${eventTypeId}]`).first().hover();
await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
await expect(tooltip).toHaveText("Open options");
```

`tooltip` is defined once as "any element matching `[role="tooltip"]` anywhere on the page," and that same locator is reused for both assertions.

**Why that's fragile:** Radix's `Tooltip` renders its content into a `Portal`, and — since `Tooltip.tsx` doesn't set `disableHoverableContent` — it closes via Radix's `Presence` mechanism, which supports an animated exit rather than an instant DOM removal. So when you hover away from the preview button onto the ellipsis button, there's a real window where the *first* tooltip's content node can still be present in the DOM (mid-unmount) at the exact moment the *second* tooltip is opening. During that window, `page.locator('[role="tooltip"]')` resolves to **two** elements instead of one.

Playwright locators are strict-mode by default: an assertion like `.toBeVisible()` or `.toHaveText()` requires the locator to resolve to exactly one element, or it throws a "strict mode violation: resolved to 2 elements" error. That's the most likely reason the test would intermittently fail — a timing race, not a real product bug (which is also why the two research agents found no functional break in either the ref-forwarding fix or the `tooltip`-prop composition).

**Why scoping the locator fixes it, not just masks it:**

```ts
await expect(page.locator('[role="tooltip"]', { hasText: "Preview" })).toBeVisible();
...
await expect(page.locator('[role="tooltip"]', { hasText: "Open options" })).toBeVisible();
```

Instead of asking "is there exactly one tooltip on the page right now," each assertion asks "is there a tooltip with *this specific text* visible." Even if a stale, still-unmounting tooltip from the previous hover briefly coexists with the new one, the two now have different text, so each locator uniquely and deterministically resolves to one element regardless of the exact timing of Radix's exit animation. It removes the race condition instead of just adding a wait that could still flake under different timing.

Want me to write this into the plan file now and move on to applying it?

Two occurrences (desktop ~line 672-679, mobile ~line 748) of the `<Button ... StartIcon="ellipsis" />` inside `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`.

**Must use `Button`'s `tooltip` prop directly here, NOT the external `<Tooltip>` wrap** used elsewhere in this file — even though the wrap is this file's usual convention for standalone buttons. Reason: this button is the immediate child of `DropdownMenuTrigger asChild`, which clones its child and injects a `ref` + props (`onClick`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, etc.) onto it so Radix can wire up the dropdown. `Tooltip` (`packages/ui/components/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx`) is a plain function component, not `forwardRef`, and it only forwards its extra props to `TooltipPrimitive.Content` (the bubble), never to `children` (the trigger) — so wrapping `<Tooltip><Button/></Tooltip>` here would silently break `DropdownMenuTrigger`'s ref/click-handling, the same bug class we just fixed in `Button`, but for the dropdown menu instead. `Button`'s `tooltip` prop avoids this because `Button` is a proper `forwardRef` component that spreads injected props and the ref straight onto the real `<button>` element before wrapping it in its own internal tooltip — matching the working precedent at `packages/features/schedules/components/DateOverrideList.tsx:128-133` (`<DialogTrigger asChild><Button tooltip={t("edit")} .../></DialogTrigger>`).

No explicit `tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset`, so it defaults to `top`, matching the rest of the row:

```tsx
tooltip={t("open_options")}
```

No new translation needed — `"open_options": "Open options"` already exists at `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json:900`.

## Tests

### Unit test — `packages/ui/components/button/button.test.tsx`

Note: the existing test suites in this file are entirely wrapped in `describe.skip(...)` (there's a `TODO: (SEAN) Fix tests for button component` comment saying they're broken due to a vitest/RTL version change). A new test added inside those skipped blocks would silently never run. So: add a **new, separate, non-skipped `describe` block** specifically for this regression, rather than touching the existing skipped suites (out of scope to fix those here).

Test: render `<Button href="/test" ref={ref} />` with a `React.createRef<HTMLAnchorElement>()`, assert `ref.current` is a real anchor element (e.g. `ref.current?.tagName === "A"`). This is a DOM-structure/ref assertion, which jsdom handles reliably — unlike tooltip *visibility*, which depends on real layout that jsdom doesn't compute (this is part of why the bug shipped silently in the first place).

### E2E test — `apps/web/playwright/event-types.e2e.ts`

Add a small test: go to `/event-types`, hover the preview button (`data-testid="preview-link-button"`) and assert a tooltip with the expected text becomes visible; same for the ellipsis button (`data-testid="event-type-options-${id}"`). This is a new pattern for this test file/repo — no existing test to copy verbatim — so write it using Playwright's standard `locator.hover()` + `page.getByRole("tooltip")`/text assertion.

## E2E regression investigation (in progress)

After implementing the plan above, running the e2e suite surfaced 4 failures: our new hover test, plus 3 previously-passing tests (`event-types.e2e.ts` "edit first event", `event-types.e2e.ts` "Different Locations Tests > can select 'display on booking page' option...", and `booking-pages.e2e.ts` "can reschedule a booking"). Investigating whether these are caused by the `Button.tsx` ref-forwarding fix, or unrelated/flaky, or a fragile new test.

### Finding: `booking-pages.e2e.ts` "can reschedule a booking" — no plausible connection

- The reschedule dropdown trigger (`BookingActionsDropdown.tsx:544-553`) is a `Button` with **no `href`** → untouched non-link branch.
- The `[data-testid="reschedule"]` item renders via `DropdownItem` → `ButtonOrLink` (`packages/ui/components/dropdown/Dropdown.tsx:181-191`), which explicitly strips `ref` before rendering `next/link` (`const { ref: _ref, ...linkProps } = props`) — bypasses `Button` entirely, so our fix can't reach it.
- The shared `confirmReschedule()` helper is used by 10+ other reschedule tests across other e2e files; none of those failed, which would be expected if the shared flow were actually broken.
- Conclusion: looks like the documented pre-existing-flaky case (`agents/rules/ci-check-failures.md`), not a regression. Plan: rerun this one test in isolation to confirm before spending more time on it.

### Finding: our new hover test (`event-types.e2e.ts:54`) — selector is fragile, likely a test bug not a product bug

- `[role="tooltip"]` is reused as a single locator across two sequential `.hover()` calls with no wait/dismiss between them. Radix's `Tooltip` doesn't set `disableHoverableContent`, and unmounts via Presence (animated exit) — if the first tooltip's content node is still present when the second hover fires, the locator can resolve to 2 elements and Playwright's strict-mode `.toBeVisible()` throws. This is the most likely failure mode.
- No functional reason found for the tooltip to fail to open at all (Radix's hover detection is driven by cloned pointer-event handlers, not by the ref we changed).
- **Fix plan:** scope each assertion to the specific tooltip content instead of reusing one bare `[role="tooltip"]` locator — e.g. `page.locator('[role="tooltip"]', { hasText: "Preview" })`, or explicitly wait for the first tooltip to close (hover away / `toBeHidden()`) before hovering the second target.

### Finding: "edit first event" and "Different Locations Tests" — no plausible connection to either diff

Traced both tests' exact click paths against both commits:

- **"edit first event"**: clicks `[data-testid=event-types] > li a`, which is a **raw Next.js `<Link>`** (`event-types-listing-view.tsx:234`), not the shared `Button` component at all — unaffected by the `Button.tsx` change. Then clicks `[data-testid=update-eventtype]` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:274-283`), a `Button` with no `href` (`type="submit"`) — goes through the `<button>` branch of `Button.tsx`, whose `ref={forwardedRef}` was **already present before our commit** (verified via `git show 6d3c0e89f3` — the diff only touches the `isLink`/`<Link>` branch).
- **"Different Locations Tests > can select 'display on booking page'..."**: same raw `<Link>` navigation via `gotoFirstEventType()`, then only touches `location-select`, `add-location` (non-`href` `Button`), `delete-locations.N.type` (a raw `<button>`, not the shared component), and checkboxes. No `href`-`Button` anywhere in its path.
- Neither test ever clicks the two ellipsis buttons that got the new `tooltip` prop either.
- `ArrowButton` (event reordering) is a plain raw `<button>`, not the shared `Button` — irrelevant. `useAutoAnimate`'s ref is on the `<ul>` itself, unrelated to `Button` internals.

**Conclusion across all 3 non-new failures (reschedule, edit first event, different locations): no interacted element traces back to either diff.** Combined with the reschedule test's shared `confirmReschedule()` helper passing in 10+ other tests, this points to pre-existing flakiness / an environment issue, not a regression from this PR. Per `agents/rules/ci-check-failures.md` ("E2E tests can be flaky... focus only on CI failures directly related to your code changes"), the recommended next step is rerunning these 3 tests in isolation (and ideally on `main`, unmodified) to confirm they fail independently of this branch — not to keep chasing a code-level cause that two independent traces couldn't find.

### Answering: would switching the preview button to the `tooltip` prop (instead of the `<Tooltip>` wrapper) help?

No — for two independent reasons:

1. **It wouldn't work at all.** The preview button has `href`, so it renders through `Button`'s `isLink` branch, which returns directly without ever going through `Wrapper` (the code that reads the `tooltip`/`tooltipSide`/`tooltipOffset` props and renders a `Tooltip`). Passing `tooltip="..."` to an `href`-`Button` is silently a no-op — this was the exact reason the wrapper pattern exists in the first place. Switching would just reintroduce the original "tooltip renders in JSX but never shows" bug, not fix anything.
2. **It wouldn't address the actual failure mode found.** Both the prop-based and wrapper-based paths ultimately render the same underlying `packages/ui/components/tooltip/Tooltip.tsx` → Radix `Tooltip.Content` markup (`role="tooltip"`). The hover test's fragility (see below) is a **test-locator problem** — reusing one bare `[role="tooltip"]` locator across two sequential hovers with no wait for the first tooltip to unmount — not a difference in which Button API produced the markup.

### Fix: scope the hover test's tooltip locator per assertion

`event-types.e2e.ts`'s new test (~line 54-69) currently does:
```ts
const tooltip = page.locator('[role="tooltip"]');
await page.locator("[data-testid=preview-link-button]").first().hover();
await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
await expect(tooltip).toHaveText("Preview");
await page.locator(`[data-testid=event-type-options-${eventTypeId}]`).first().hover();
await expect(tooltip).toBeVisible();
await expect(tooltip).toHaveText("Open options");
```
If the first tooltip's content is still present (Radix's Presence-based animated unmount) when the second `.hover()` fires, `[role="tooltip"]` can resolve to 2 elements and Playwright's strict-mode `.toBeVisible()`/`.toHaveText()` throws. Fix: scope each assertion to its own expected text instead of reusing one generic locator, e.g. `page.locator('[role="tooltip"]', { hasText: "Preview" })` per hover, so each assertion is unambiguous even if a stale tooltip is still unmounting.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 09:52:11Z)**_

That failure is very informative — the "Preview" assertion passed silently (no error before line 66), and only "Open options" times out completely (`element(s) not found`, not "hidden"), meaning that tooltip never mounts at all. I dug into the actual Radix Tooltip source (`node_modules/@radix-ui/react-tooltip`) to find out why, and I don't think this is a `DropdownMenuTrigger` composition bug after all — it's something more fundamental about how the test chains two hovers together.

**What I found:** this app wraps its entire tree in a single global `<TooltipProvider>` (`apps/web/lib/app-providers-app-dir.tsx:104`). That provider holds one shared `isPointerInTransitRef` used by *every* tooltip on the page. Radix's tooltips are "hoverable" by default (`disableHoverableContent` isn't set), which means when you move the pointer away from an open tooltip's trigger, Radix doesn't close it immediately — it tracks a "grace area" polygon between the trigger and the bubble, and only closes once the pointer is confirmed to have left that zone, updating the shared `isPointerInTransitRef` flag as it goes (`TooltipTrigger`, line 196 of the source):

```js
onPointerMove: composeEventHandlers(props.onPointerMove, (event) => {
  if (event.pointerType === 'touch') return;
  if (!hasPointerMoveOpenedRef.current && !providerContext.isPointerInTransitRef.current) {
    context.onTriggerEnter();
    ...
```

A brand-new trigger's tooltip only opens if `isPointerInTransitRef.current` is `false` at the moment its `onPointerMove` fires. My hypothesis: hovering "Preview" opens its tooltip and puts the shared provider into "hoverable/transit" bookkeeping; when the test immediately calls `.hover()` on the ellipsis button right after, Playwright's synthetic hover can land before Radix's own pointer-tracking has settled that flag back to `false`. If no further pointer movement happens after that (which is exactly what a single programmatic `.hover()` does — it doesn't keep moving), the ellipsis tooltip's `onTriggerEnter()` is never called again, and it never opens — permanently, matching your 120s timeout exactly. This would apply to any two chained hover-tooltip assertions on this page, unrelated to the `DropdownMenuTrigger` nesting I originally worried about.

I'd like to fix this by decoupling the two checks rather than chaining them, so there's no shared-state race between assertions.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 09:53:28Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the hover test avoid the shared-TooltipProvider race between the two chained hovers?**

Options:
- **Split into two separate tests (Recommended)** - One test hovers only the preview button, another hovers only the ellipsis button. Each starts with a fresh page load, so there's no leftover 'pointer in transit' state from a prior tooltip to race against.
- **Reset pointer state between hovers in one test** - Keep one test, but explicitly move the mouse to a neutral point and wait for the first tooltip to become hidden before hovering the second target. More fragile — still timing-dependent on Radix's own grace-area logic, which we don't fully control.


**Answer:** Split into two separate tests (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 14:58:30Z)**_

This is a pre-existing environment issue, not something caused by our diff — we never touched anything under `packages/app-store`, and the error itself (`spawn tsc ENOENT`) is a tooling/PATH resolution failure, not a TypeScript compile error in any code.

**What's likely happening:** `packages/app-store`'s `type-check:ci` script runs `tsc-absolute --pretty --noEmit` (a thin wrapper around `tsc` that rewrites reported paths to absolute ones). That wrapper internally spawns a plain `tsc` process. `tsc`/`tsc.cmd` does exist in the repo root's `node_modules/.bin`, but `packages/app-store` has no local `node_modules/.bin` of its own (normal for a hoisted yarn workspace) — so this only works if the root's `node_modules/.bin` is on `PATH` when Turbo spawns that task from inside `packages/app-store`'s working directory. On Windows, it looks like it isn't in this case, so the `tsc` lookup fails with `ENOENT`.

**What I'd try, in order:**

1. **Scope the type-check to just the packages we actually touched**, skipping the broken `app-store` package entirely — this is really the more relevant check for our PR anyway:
   ```bash
   yarn turbo run type-check:ci --filter=@calcom/ui --filter=@calcom/web --force
   ```

2. **Confirm it's really an environment quirk and not something specific to `--force`/Turbo's process spawning**, by running that one package's script directly instead of through Turbo:
   ```bash
   cd packages/app-store && yarn type-check:ci
   ```
   If that also fails with the same `ENOENT`, it's a local machine/tooling setup issue (worth its own investigation someday, but unrelated to this PR). If it works fine standalone, it's specifically Turbo's spawn/PATH handling on your machine.

Either way, since `packages/app-store` isn't part of our diff, I wouldn't block on fixing this — the `--filter` command in step 1 is the one that actually verifies our changes.

Good catch running it broader — this confirms it: the exact same `spawn tsc ENOENT` fails identically for both `@calcom/ui` and `@calcom/web`. That rules out anything specific to `packages/app-store` or to our diff — this is a general, environment-wide problem with the `type-check:ci` script on this machine, not something introduced by our branch.

**Likely cause:** `type-check:ci` runs through `tsc-absolute`, a wrapper that internally calls Node's `child_process.spawn('tsc', [...])` directly. On Windows, the actual installed binary is `tsc.cmd` (a shim), and `child_process.spawn()` without `shell: true` does **not** automatically resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` extensions the way a real shell would — Windows' `CreateProcess` needs an exact filename match. That's a known cross-platform gotcha for CLI wrappers that don't use a library like `cross-spawn` to handle it. Plain `yarn <script>` invocations don't have this problem because yarn's own script runner already shells out correctly — which is why the plain `type-check` script (not `:ci`) should work fine.

**Try this instead**, which does the identical type-check but skips the broken wrapper:
```bash
yarn turbo run type-check --filter=@calcom/ui --filter=@calcom/web --force
```

This runs `tsc --pretty --noEmit` directly (via yarn, which handles the `.cmd` shim correctly) instead of going through `tsc-absolute`. You lose the "rewrite to absolute paths" convenience in the output, but the actual type errors reported will be identical — that's the only thing `tsc-absolute` adds. If this passes cleanly, our changes are type-safe, and the `:ci` variant's failure is just a pre-existing local tooling quirk on this machine (would be worth reporting separately, but it's not blocking here and isn't specific to this branch).

In the cal.diy repo, on this user's Windows machine, `yarn type-check:ci --force` reliably fails with `Error: spawn tsc ENOENT` for every package it touches (confirmed identically for `@calcom/app-store`, `@calcom/ui`, and `@calcom/web`). This is not caused by any particular branch or code change — it reproduces the same way regardless of what files were edited.

The root cause is that each package's `type-check:ci` script runs through `tsc-absolute` (a wrapper that rewrites TypeScript's reported paths to absolute paths), which internally calls Node's `child_process.spawn('tsc', [...])` directly rather than through a cross-platform-safe spawner. On Windows, the installed binary is actually `tsc.cmd`, and `child_process.spawn()` without `shell: true` does not resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` extensions the way a real shell does, so the spawn fails to find `tsc` at all.

The plain `type-check` script (without `:ci`) runs `tsc --pretty --noEmit` directly via `yarn`, which correctly resolves the `.cmd` shim, and reports the same underlying type errors — it just skips the absolute-path rewriting convenience. So on this machine, prefer:

```bash
yarn turbo run type-check --filter=<package> --force
```

over `yarn type-check:ci --force`, when verifying type safety in this repo. This has been confirmed to actually run and pass on this machine, whereas `type-check:ci` cannot be used at all until the underlying `tsc-absolute`/Windows spawn issue is fixed upstream or worked around in the repo's tooling.

**Title:**

feat(event-types): add tooltips to preview and dropdown-menu buttons

**Body:**
```markdown
## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #16

Adds tooltips to the remaining icon-only action buttons on the Event Types list page (`/event-types`) that didn't already have them — the "preview" (view event) button and the "..." dropdown-menu button — matching the tooltips already present on the hide/show toggle and copy-link buttons in the same row.

While implementing this, we found the preview button's tooltip was actually broken in dev/prod despite already being wrapped in `<Tooltip>`: `Button` never forwarded its `ref` to the underlying `<a>` when rendered with `href`, so Radix's `Tooltip` had no real DOM node to anchor/position itself against and silently never displayed. That's fixed here too (`packages/ui/components/button/Button.tsx`), since the dropdown-menu tooltip's correctness also depends on it.

Out of scope: `EventTypeLayout.tsx` (the single event-type edit page) has an unrelated, pre-existing bug — a hardcoded, untranslated `"Link copied!"` toast string. Tracked separately, not fixed here.

## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

<!-- TODO: add before/after screenshots or a short screen recording showing the preview and "..." button tooltips on /event-types -->

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [ ] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- [x] I have updated the developer docs if this PR makes changes that would require a documentation change. N/A — no developer-facing docs cover this behavior.
- [x] I confirm automated tests are in place that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.

## How should this be tested?

- No new environment variables required.
- Minimal test data: any account with at least one event type.
